svg.text: Pharmacy Access Study: Background, Methods, Results, Limitations and Future Work

g.text: • Pharmacy deserts are areas where residents must travel more than 1 mile (urban) or 10 miles (rural) to reach a pharmacy
• We surveyed 412 residents across 6 neighborhoods between March and June using a mixed-methods approach with follow-up interviews
• Average walking distance: 1.4 mi (N), 0.6 mi (S), 2.1 mi (E), 0.9 mi (W), 1.7 mi (C), 1.2 mi (NE) — see appendix table 4
• 38% reported skipping a prescription in the past year; 61% of those cited distance; 22% cost; 17% hours; 9% other reasons
• Limitations: self-reported data, seasonal effects, survey language, sampling frame, response rate of 41%
Fig. 3 distances by area (mi) n=412 p<.05
Future work: expand to 3 more cities, add GPS tracking,
partner with clinics, test delivery pilot, policy brief,
cost model, community advisory board, IRB amendment
Sources: County health dept. 2025; Smith et al. 2024; Lee 2023;
Census ACS 2024; internal survey data; pharmacy registry 2025
